title: Why Does God Allow Evil?
content: The Bible teaches that evil entered the world through human sin. In the beginning, God created a good world, but humanity's rebellion introduced sin, suffering, and death. God created humans with free will so that love and obedience could be genuine choices. Evil is therefore not created by God but results from the misuse of human freedom. Scripture also teaches that God allows evil temporarily while working toward a greater purpose and will ultimately remove evil completely.

title: Why Do Good People Suffer?
content: The Bible explains that suffering affects all humanity because the world has been corrupted by sin. However, suffering is not always a punishment for personal wrongdoing. Scripture shows that God can use suffering to develop perseverance, deepen faith, and accomplish purposes that may not be immediately understood. The experiences of Job and the teachings of the apostles demonstrate that God remains present even in suffering.

title: Does Suffering Disprove God?
content: The existence of evil does not logically disprove the existence of God. In fact, calling something 'evil' assumes an objective moral standard. Christianity teaches that this moral standard ultimately comes from God. The Bible acknowledges the reality of suffering but also provides an explanation through the fall of humanity and offers hope through redemption in Christ.

title: God's Justice and Final Judgment
content: Christian teaching affirms that God will ultimately judge evil and establish perfect justice. Temporary injustice in the present world does not mean that evil will go unpunished. Scripture teaches that a final judgment will occur, where God will hold every person accountable and establish righteousness forever.
